contracts: _activate() returns repo_task_memories: list[dict] in its state-update dict alongside the existing task_memories

hooks/dispatcher.py's _format_system_prompt renders repo_task_memories under a separate '## Repo memories' section, and _enforce_context_budget counts its tokens toward the shared budget (added after a concept-audit catch, see dispatcher-system-prompt-assembly)
activate-task-memory-source-selection.description: On task activation (tasks__set_active/tasks__pop_active), ActivateTaskNode selects the source of task-context memories based on whether the active task's cwd has migrated to the repo_memory split (task:850ddd65): if <cwd>/repo_memory/memories.json exists, the global _score_memories() scorer is skipped entirely and repo_task_memories (filtered by the task's Files: section overlap via backfill_memory_files.py's _file_tokens stem-matching) is used instead. If no repo_memory store exists for that cwd, falls back to the pre-split behavior (global MEMORY.sqlite scoring, unfiltered by Files:). The two sources are mutually exclusive per activation, never both populated for the same task. This concept only covers the memory-source-selection behavior, not activate_task.py's other responsibilities (execution_contract building, task_stack push/pop, task lookup).
invariants: repo_store_path presence (not emptiness) is the switch — an existing-but-empty repo_memory/memories.json still skips the global scorer, it doesn't fall back
task_memories and repo_task_memories are never both non-empty for the same activation
Absence of a Files: section on the task means ALL repo_memory entries are returned unfiltered (intentional — the store is small/curated, unlike the global table, so no-filter is not noise)
tasks__pop_active on an empty stack clears both task_memories and repo_task_memories alongside the other active-task fields
activate-task-memory-source-selection.name: activate-task-memory-source-selection

contracts: record_commit(task_id, commit_hash, repo_path="") -> {ok, task_id, commit_hash} or {error}
handle_get_commits(task_id) -> list of {commit_hash, repo_path, logged_at}, most recent first
commit-task-traceability-capture.description: commit_task_map table (task_id, commit_hash, repo_path, logged_at; UNIQUE(task_id, commit_hash)) records which commit SHA implemented which task, populated post-commit by hooks/dispatcher.py (_record_bash_commit for Bash git-commit calls, _record_mcp_commit for the MCP git__commit tool from any server), queryable via the tasks__get_commits MCP tool (handle_get_commits). Complements GitCommitGate/gates-commit-traceability, which only enforces task:<id> presence pre-commit — this concept is the post-commit half that closes the loop.
invariants: INSERT OR IGNORE via the UNIQUE(task_id, commit_hash) constraint makes recording idempotent — safe to call twice for the same commit

record_commit() returns an error dict (never raises) if task_id is unknown or either field is empty; both dispatcher capture functions treat any failure as fail-open (log a warning, never block the tool response)
Table name deliberately avoids task_commits — that name was already used (and removed) for an unrelated LangGraph checkpoint-state key (task:c5628e95)
commit-task-traceability-capture.name: commit-task-traceability-capture

invariants: cwd_domains.json (icloud_db_dir, same pattern as memory_scoring.json) is the source of truth for repo-to-domain classification — add an entry there when onboarding a repo, no code change/redeploy needed
_CWD_DOMAIN_MAP_DEFAULT is only a fallback seed, used if cwd_domains.json is missing or fails to parse
Config is frozen (immutable after construction)

evidence: src/tools/tasks.py: _ensure_db() executes OPEN_TASKS_DDL/TASK_EVENTS_DDL/TASK_EDGES_DDL/COMMIT_TASK_MAP_DDL and calls migrate_tasks_db() directly (task:1310d3a3) — proj_tasks.db is no longer an exception
invariants: All migrations are additive-only (ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN) — never destructive
migrate_*() functions are safe to run repeatedly (idempotent)

DDL constants ARE the authoritative schema definition for every DB this module covers, including proj_tasks.db (task:1310d3a3 reversed the task:1219383a-era exception — src/tools/tasks.py's _ensure_db() now executes these DDL constants and calls migrate_tasks_db() directly rather than maintaining a parallel copy). The one nuance: proj_tasks.db's VALUE backfills (keywords, parent_id-from-tags) and status normalization stay in src/tools/tasks.py itself, since they depend on tasks.py's own helper functions and moving them here would create a circular import — schema.py owns structure (what columns exist), tasks.py owns those specific backfills (what values populate them). See tasks-db-schema-and-migration for the full detail.

contracts: Reads hook payload from stdin, writes JSON to stdout
Returns additionalSystemPrompt for UserPromptSubmit
Returns permissionDecision=deny for blocked PreToolUse
PreToolUse handlers may also return permissionDecision=allow with additionalContext to inject a non-blocking reminder into Claude's context without denying the tool call
dispatcher-hook-event-routing.description: Single entry point for all Claude Code hook events. Routes each event type (UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionStart, SessionEnd) to its dedicated handler via a dispatch table.
invariants: Every hook event must map to exactly one handler in _HANDLERS
PreToolUse handlers that fail on irreversible tools must deny, not allow
Handlers return None to pass through or a dict with hookSpecificOutput to act

Two distinct PreToolUse response categories: gates (deny-capable checks like _check_task_body_format, run_gate) must resolve to a strict allow/deny decision; reminders (like _maybe_drift_reflection_nudge for Write/Edit/MultiEdit) are allow-only and use additionalContext to surface non-blocking context — reminders never deny

Two distinct handler return shapes exist: PreToolUse/UserPromptSubmit handlers return None or a dict wrapping hookSpecificOutput; Stop handlers (_handle_stop) return None or a plain top-level {"decision": "block", "reason": ...} dict per Claude Code's Stop-hook schema (not wrapped in hookSpecificOutput). The turn-completion chime no longer uses Stop-hook blocking: since 150df2a the sound plays server-side via PlaySoundNode (detached afplay subprocess, start_new_session=True — no Claude round-trip). NoopNode marks the first Stop of a turn by setting state['stop_alert_sent']=True, which gates PlaySoundNode (next node in the stop chain) so the chime fires exactly once per turn; sound_played guards replays within the same turn, and run_session() resets stop_alert_sent=False on the next UserPromptSubmit. run_stop() in session_graph.py still surfaces-and-clears pending_hook_output for any node that sets one (task:aacf3ef3 history; refactored by 150df2a).

PostToolUse also runs unconditional side-effect capture functions before the mcp__-prefix gate: _record_bash_commit (Bash tool, matches _GIT_COMMIT_RE/_TASK_ID_RE, shells out to git rev-parse HEAD) and _record_mcp_commit (short_name == "git__commit" from any MCP server, reads commit_sha directly from tool_response). Both call src.tools.tasks.record_commit() to insert into commit_task_map — a direct dispatcher-level function call, not a LangGraph node, and not routed through the __hook__/mcp_hook_bridge convention (that convention is one-way, prompt-injection only, no side effects). task:a2fd402d
dispatcher-hook-event-routing.name: dispatcher-hook-event-routing

contracts: Returns a string (may be empty) to be injected as additionalSystemPrompt
All sections are markdown-formatted
dispatcher-system-prompt-assembly.description: Assembles the UserPromptSubmit additionalSystemPrompt from SessionState context (memories, task context, repo memories, related tasks/commits, rag chunks) into markdown sections, applying a token budget before rendering.
invariants: Sections are only emitted when their data is non-empty

Related tasks section is populated when LoadRelatedTasksNode finds semantically similar done tasks via TurboVec neighbor search (capped at 3); empty when no active task, no rag index, or no matching done neighbors
Task context summary takes precedence over raw task history when both exist

New-project note is emitted when ctx['cwd_unmapped'] is true (set by CwdDomainDetectNode only on the first turn a session's cwd is unmapped, tracked via cwd_domain_reminder_sent in checkpoint state so it fires once per session, not every turn)

Before assembly, _enforce_context_budget(ctx) trims ctx['memories'] from the tail (lowest-scored, since the list is pre-sorted descending) until the combined token count of memories+task_memories+repo_task_memories+related_tasks+related_commits+task_rag_chunks fits _CONTEXT_TOKEN_BUDGET (4000 tokens), or memories is empty. task_memories/repo_task_memories/related_tasks/related_commits/task_rag_chunks are counted toward the budget but never trimmed themselves — they're already small/capped by their producing nodes (repo_task_memories is filtered by Files: overlap at task-activation time, task:850ddd65).

task_body is hard-truncated to _TASK_BODY_CHAR_CAP (3000 chars) at render time, appending an "...[truncated]" marker when cut — it has no upstream length cap (a task's body can be arbitrarily long, e.g. a large epic scaffold).

mid_task_decisions (Task decisions section) is capped to the most recent _MAX_DECISIONS (15) entries by langchain_learning/nodes/decision_task.py, sliced on every tasks__add_decision append — not trimmed in dispatcher.py itself. This checkpoint state exists solely for prompt injection; the durable decision history lives in the task's DB record, unaffected by the slice.

execution_contract is rendered as its own section, independent of task_body and _enforce_context_budget — it is NOT subject to _TASK_BODY_CHAR_CAP truncation or memories-budget eviction, by design (a fixed north-star template built once at task activation by activate_task.py._build_execution_contract, must stay byte-identical every turn). Cleared alongside the other active-task fields at all three deactivation sites: DeactivateTaskNode (tasks__clear_active/tasks__finish), ActivateTaskNode's pop-to-empty-stack, and LogTaskEventsNode's "task:<id> done" auto-close (task:eb46ac47 — this third site was originally missed).

After _format_system_prompt, the UPS handler appends one-shot node output: if ctx['pending_hook_output'].hookSpecificOutput has hookEventName == 'UserPromptSubmit', its additionalContext is appended to the assembled system prompt (e.g. LogTaskEventsNode's /task-introspection nudge after a "task:<id> done" auto-close, task:eb46ac47). run_session() surfaces-and-clears the checkpoint copy (mirroring run_post_tool/run_stop), so the payload renders exactly once and cannot leak into the next PostToolUse response; the hookEventName gate prevents a stale cross-event payload from ever being rendered here.

repo_task_memories (## Repo memories section) is emitted alongside task_memories (## Task memories) but the two are mutually exclusive in practice per-repo: activate_task.py sources task_memories from either the global scorer OR repo_memory, never both, depending on whether the active task's repo has migrated to repo_memory/memories.json (task:850ddd65).
dispatcher-system-prompt-assembly.name: dispatcher-system-prompt-assembly

invariants: task_templates/*.md is the single source of truth for required sections
Gate only applies to claude-hooks domain tasks (other domains pass through)
Gate runs before JiraHierarchyGate in the PreToolUse chain

invariants: Every commit must reference task:<id> in the command string
Non-commit Bash calls are never blocked by this gate

gates-jira-hierarchy.description: Enforces Jira-style parent-child issue type rules on tasks__create. Stories/tasks/bugs must have epic parents; subtasks must have story/task/bug parents; epics cannot have parents. validate_jira_hierarchy() is the single source of truth shared with the UI.

contracts: check(tool, ctx) returns (deny: bool, reason: str)
deny=True means the tool must be blocked; reason is shown to Claude
gates-prereq-chain-enforcement.description: Anti-hallucination send-gate system. Verifies tool calls against session history before allowing them. Each gate is a composable chain of verifier factories loaded from gate_rules.yaml or hardcoded subclasses.
invariants: Gates operate only on tool call records written by the hook infrastructure, never on model memory
External gate rules from gate_rules.yaml never override internal Python gates
All gates fail open on DB errors — a broken gate never blocks tools
gates-prereq-chain-enforcement.name: gates-prereq-chain-enforcement

contracts: Callers reading hook_logs (e.g. hooks__read_logs_sqlite MCP tool) should treat it as a rolling ~40-50k row window of recent activity, not a complete historical log -- older entries are permanently gone once pruned, not archived.
hook-logs-sqlite-autoprune-at-50k.description: SQLiteHandler.emit() writes every log record to hook_logs in claude_hooks.sqlite (iCloud-synced), then checks COUNT(*) on every single insert. Once the table reaches 50,000 rows, it prunes down to the newest 40,000 rows in one DELETE, keyed by ts DESC (not id DESC).
invariants: hook_logs is capped at 50,000 rows -- it auto-prunes to 40,000 on the insert that crosses the threshold, so the table oscillates between ~40k and 50k rows over time, never growing unbounded.
Pruning keeps the newest rows by ts (timestamp), not by id/rowid -- id values become non-contiguous after a prune, so id (or max(id)) is not a valid proxy for total row count or table age.

The COUNT(*) check runs on every emit() call (every log line), not on a schedule/batch -- this is an O(n) check per write, acceptable at this volume but a scaling consideration if log volume grows sharply.
Pruning is silent -- emit() swallows all exceptions (bare except: pass), so a failed prune or count-check never surfaces as an error.
hook-logs-sqlite-autoprune-at-50k.name: hook-logs-sqlite-autoprune-at-50k

contracts: Usage: python3 client.py <HookEvent>
Reads hook payload JSON from stdin, POSTs to {CLAUDE_HOOKS_SERVER or http://127.0.0.1:8766}/hook/{EVENT}, prints the response JSON to stdout
Prints 'claude-hooks: client.py invoked for {EVENT}' to stderr on every invocation, regardless of success/failure
hooks-client-cwd-forwarding.description: Thin HTTP client for the FastAPI hook server. Reads the hook JSON payload from stdin (which already carries the real per-session cwd from Claude Code) and POSTs it to localhost:8766/hook/{event}.
invariants: CLAUDE_CWD env var is a fallback only, used when payload['cwd'] from stdin is missing/empty — it must never unconditionally overwrite a cwd Claude Code already supplied, since CLAUDE_CWD reflects whatever cwd the long-running server process happened to launch from, not the calling session's cwd (bug found 2026-07-08: unconditional overwrite clobbered every session's reported cwd with a stale/empty env var)
Fails open: if the server is unreachable, exits 0 with an empty JSON object rather than blocking the hook event

Every invocation prints a one-line 'claude-hooks: client.py invoked for {EVENT}' announcement to stderr immediately after EVENT is resolved, unconditionally (before the try/except) — this exists because server-side dispatcher logs only show the server's view, giving no signal that client.py itself ran for a given hook event (task:fb7d3777)
hooks-client-cwd-forwarding.name: hooks-client-cwd-forwarding

contracts: handle_server_memory(n_events) returns a markdown table or {error: ...}
handle_read_logs_sqlite(level, logger, search, limit, format="toon") returns a TOON-encoded string by default ("count: N\nrows[N]{...}:\n  ..."), or {count, rows} dict when format="json"
handle_session_id() returns {session_id, turn} or {error: ...} after one retry on empty first response

handle_checkpoint_query(thread_id="") returns {thread_id, turn_count, prompt_id, domains, keywords, memories, tool_hints, session_context, ...} or {error: ...}; thread_id doubles as session_id, omitted thread_id resolves to the current session via GET /session/current
hooks-mcp-tools-observability.description: MCP tools for querying hook state: server_memory (live chronological timeline via HTTP), checkpoint_query (thin HTTP wrapper over the live server's GET /session/{session_id}, reading in-process MemorySaver state — no longer a SQLite reader as of task:da29c842), and read_logs_sqlite (filtered log reader from claude_hooks.sqlite). Also session_id (added 2026-07-05, task:61703ef7): returns current session_id via GET /session/current with a built-in one-shot retry, absorbing the checkpoint-write race for a brand-new session.
evidence: tests/test_checkpoint_query_integration.py: live smoke test against the real running server
invariants: server_memory hits the live FastAPI server at 127.0.0.1:8766 — fails if server is down
read_logs_sqlite reads directly from iCloud DB path
session_id retries once (0.5s sleep) if the first /session/current response has no session_id — absorbs the race where a brand-new session's first checkpoint write lags behind the query

checkpoint_query is a thin HTTP wrapper over GET /session/{session_id} — it does NOT read ~/.claude/langgraph_checkpoints.db directly (that sqlite path was retired in production by task:b3964f85; the prior invariant here claiming checkpoint_query reads that file as 'the live DB SqliteSaver writes to in production' was true when confirmed 2026-07-05 (task:61703ef7) but went stale after task:b3964f85's later migration — corrected 2026-07-27, task:da29c842, after the stale assumption caused an unhandled 'no such table: checkpoints' error). checkpoint_query has no 'latest checkpoint across all threads' mode anymore — omitted thread_id resolves only to the current session, matching hooks__session_id's semantics.

read_logs_sqlite's `format` param defaults to "toon" (task:d2165715): rows share a uniform schema (id, ts, level, logger, message), which TOON's tabular header+rows encoding compresses well versus repeating JSON keys per row. format="json" is kept as an explicit fallback returning the original {count, rows} dict shape — callers needing the dict shape (e.g. programmatic filtering) must pass format="json" explicitly.

The TOON encoder itself (rows_to_toon/toon_cell) was extracted to src/toon.py (task:4b5bf21f) so src/tools/tasks.py's handle_list could reuse it — hooks.py now imports rows_to_toon rather than defining its own copy.

A docstring/comment's 'confirmed on <date>' claim is only as fresh as the last re-check against the code it describes — checkpoint_query's docstring cited a specific confirmation date (task:61703ef7) that read as settled fact but silently went stale after a later migration nobody circled back to update. Re-verify dated confirmations against current runtime behavior, don't trust the date alone.
hooks-mcp-tools-observability.name: hooks-mcp-tools-observability

emit() never raises — handleError() is a no-op
Log table is auto-trimmed to 40k rows when it exceeds 50k
Test redirect affects only the default singleton, not custom-path handlers

New tools require adding an entry to DOMAIN_MAP — no auto-discovery
Handler functions must be named handle_<action> in their module

contracts: Callers of score_memories() can add unbounded domains without any single domain silently excluding another from scoring, as long as no one domain individually exceeds batch_limit.
memory-scoring-per-domain-batch-limit.description: score_memories() fetches candidate memory rows per-domain (not one aggregate query across the whole memories table) before applying combination-signal scoring. Each distinct domain gets its own SELECT ... WHERE domain IS ? ORDER BY updated DESC LIMIT batch_limit, and the per-domain result sets are concatenated before scoring.
invariants: batch_limit (memory_scoring.json / src.config.memory_batch_limit) is a per-domain cap, not an aggregate cap across the whole memories table.
Truncation (when a domain exceeds batch_limit rows) always drops the stalest rows in that domain first, via ORDER BY updated DESC -- never an arbitrary rowid-order slice.
A small or new domain must never be starved out of the candidate pool by a large domain growing past batch_limit -- each domain is queried independently.
memory-scoring-per-domain-batch-limit.name: memory-scoring-per-domain-batch-limit

contracts: load_index(tvim_path, meta_path) returns (IdMapIndex | None, dict)

query_index(index, meta, q_vec, k) returns list[dict] with id, score, plus meta fields

invariants: Index and metadata sidecar are always written together atomically
load_index returns (None, {}) on any error — callers must handle missing index
query_index is stateless — no caching, no side effects
rag-core-turbovec-index.name: rag-core-turbovec-index

contracts: get(name) -> dict | None
list(type=None) -> list[dict], filtered by type when given
upsert(memory: dict) -> None, requires memory['name'] and valid memory['type']
search(query) -> list[dict], case-insensitive substring match across name/body/tags, ranked by match count
repo-memory-store-pattern.description: RepoMemoryStore is a JSON-backed, per-repo committed store for project/reference memories about that repo's own code/architecture, sibling to concept_store's ConceptStore (same wrapper shape, same tolerant-missing-file behavior) but an independently-evolvable class, not a shared base. Unlike the global MEMORY.sqlite table, this store is never scored per-turn by UPS — it's consulted only during task lifecycle events (task activation, task-grooming, task-introspection) via src/tools/repo_memory.py's MCP handlers (get/list/upsert/delete/search, repo required no default, mirrors concept.py's _resolve_repo convention).
invariants: Entries have no `domain` field — the repo filesystem path itself is the domain, since the file lives inside that repo
Entries have no `hit_count`/`last_hit` — nothing scores this store per-turn, so nothing needs hit tracking
upsert() validates type is 'project' or 'reference' only, raising ValueError otherwise — the one behavioral difference from ConceptStore, which has no type enum constraint
Missing file -> empty dict, no mkdir in __init__ (mkdir only happens in handle_upsert, mirroring concept.py's gap-cover for the same reason)
save() rewrites the whole file (json.dumps indent=2 sort_keys=True) on every write — no partial/incremental writes
repo-memory-store-pattern.name: repo-memory-store-pattern

contracts: POST /hook/{event} calls dispatcher handler and returns hookSpecificOutput, a top-level decision/reason dict (Stop only), or {}
GET /health returns {status: ok}
GET /session/memory returns last N events from server_memory
GET /session/current returns {session_id, turn} from the most recent checkpoint — no active task required, unlike GET /session/active
_safe_json(request) -> dict — always returns a dict, never raises; malformed/empty/missing body returns {} with a logged warning
server-fastapi-hook-server.description: Persistent FastAPI server replacing per-invocation subprocess dispatcher. Routes POST /hook/{event} to dispatcher handlers. Uses MemorySaver (in-process, in-memory LangGraph checkpointer) — does NOT survive server restarts. Replaced SqliteSaver (task:b3964f85) after two corruption incidents. Per-thread checkpoint history is capped at 5000 rows, enforced from NoopNode on every Stop event. Single uvicorn worker process, event loop is uvloop (task:53c9f817). All 6 hook endpoints parse the request body via a shared _safe_json() helper (task:33419f95) that fails open to {} on malformed/empty JSON instead of raising — matches hooks/client.py's own fail-open design.
evidence: ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.debaditya.claude-hooks-pipeline.plist: uvicorn launch args, single process, no --workers
hooks/server.py: _safe_json() — shared JSON-parse helper used by all 6 /hook/{event} endpoints
invariants: Checkpoint state lives only in-process memory (MemorySaver) — discarded on every server restart/reload; nothing about session/task-activation state persists across a restart except what server_memory.py separately logs to SQLite
Per-thread checkpoint history is capped at 5000 rows via NoopNode on every Stop event, not by the server itself
Server runs on port 8766 as a single uvicorn worker process — deliberately not multi-worker/per-session
GET /session/active and GET /session/current both read live in-memory MemorySaver state (not a DB); /session/active requires an active task, /session/current does not
Event loop is uvloop, not stdlib asyncio — controlled entirely by whether uvloop is installed

All 6 /hook/{event} endpoints (UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionStart, SessionEnd) parse their body via the shared _safe_json(request) helper, which catches any JSON-parse failure and returns {} instead of letting it propagate to the generic exception handler as a 500 — found missing (task:33419f95, log audit 2026-07-26) after an empty/malformed body crashed pre_tool_use with an unhandled JSONDecodeError. Any NEW hook endpoint added here must use _safe_json too, not a bare `await request.json()`, to preserve this fail-open guarantee.
server-fastapi-hook-server.name: server-fastapi-hook-server

contracts: record_prompt/record_tool/record_task write to both layers
get(n_events) returns from in-memory cache only (no DB hit at read time)
server-memory-consolidated-timeline.description: Two-layer consolidated context store (SQLite + in-memory cache) answering 'what was I working on?'. Stores prompts, MCP tool calls, and task activations as a chronological event sequence. Write-through: every insert hits both SQLite and the in-memory cache.
invariants: Test sessions (prefixed test-, pytest-, api-test-) are never written to the store
Rolling window capped at 1000 events — oldest deleted on overflow
Cache is hydrated from SQLite at server startup so context survives reloads
server-memory-consolidated-timeline.name: server-memory-consolidated-timeline

Bash non-VCS calls are silently skipped

contracts: get_session_graph(session_id: str = '') -> a compiled, checkpointer-backed StateGraph, production or test depending on session_id prefix
session-graph-test-production-routing.description: get_session_graph(session_id) is the single chokepoint every hook entry point (run_session, run_gate, run_post_tool, run_stop, prewarm_session) already calls to obtain the compiled LangGraph StateGraph. Since task:b63088a1, it also decides WHICH of two graph instances to return based on session_id's prefix, isolating integration-test checkpoint traffic from the shared production MemorySaver without changing any endpoint URL or code path.
invariants: Any session_id starting with TEST_SESSION_PREFIX ('integration-test-') routes to _test_graph, a separate lazily-built graph/MemorySaver instance; every other session_id (including '') routes to the production _graph, exactly as before this routing existed.

Both _graph and _test_graph are built lazily on first use via the identical build_session_graph(checkpointer=MemorySaver()) pattern — no special-casing between them except which module-level global gets populated.

A checkpoint written under a test-prefixed session_id is genuinely invisible to the production graph, not just conventionally separated — they are two distinct MemorySaver instances with independent .storage dicts.
No eviction/cleanup logic exists for _test_graph and none is needed: both graphs reset to empty on every server restart, since MemorySaver has no persistence and none is intended for either.

Callers that reference the underlying singleton directly (sg._graph) rather than through get_session_graph(session_id) will NOT get isolation-aware routing — hooks/server.py's session_detail endpoint and hooks/dispatcher.py's _handle_session_end both had to be updated to route through get_session_graph(session_id) (or check the correct global explicitly) for the isolation guarantee to hold end-to-end.
session-graph-test-production-routing.name: session-graph-test-production-routing

contracts: get_current_session() -> {session_id, turn} or {} if no checkpoint exists anywhere
get_active_session() -> {task_id, title, session_id, turn} or {} if no active task on the latest checkpoint, or that task is done/abandoned
session-state-latest-checkpoint-lookup.description: get_current_session/get_active_session back GET /session/current and GET /session/active — the only signals available for 'what session am I in' before any thread_id is known. Both use _latest_checkpoint_tuple() to find the single most-recently-written checkpoint ACROSS ALL THREADS in a MemorySaver instance.
invariants: MemorySaver.list(None) (no config) iterates checkpointer.storage's thread_ids in Python dict-insertion order, then yields that FIRST thread's own checkpoint history before ever considering other threads — next(iter(checkpointer.list(None))) is NOT 'the most recent checkpoint globally', it's 'thread_ids[0]'s own most recent checkpoint', where thread_ids[0] never changes once set (dict insertion order is stable across key updates). This was task:a4531510's root cause: a long-lived thread (from a test fixture posting a hardcoded session_id every run) permanently occupied thread_ids[0], so get_current_session got stuck returning it forever regardless of real traffic.

_latest_checkpoint_tuple() fixes this by enumerating checkpointer.storage.keys() and calling get_tuple() per thread (O(1) latest-checkpoint lookup, not full-history iteration), comparing each thread's checkpoint['ts'] ISO timestamp to find the true global latest.

get_active_session additionally filters out done/abandoned tasks even when the checkpoint itself is stale — a checkpoint with an active_task_id pointing at a closed task still yields {} from this function.
session-state-latest-checkpoint-lookup.name: session-state-latest-checkpoint-lookup

contracts: TaskDocument.to_json()/to_dict() round-trip losslessly through TaskDocument.from_json() for every field, including nested Risk.graded, IntrospectionReport.grooming_accuracy, and Implementation.total/done (tests/test_task_document.py::TestRoundTrip)
Grooming.grade_risks(grades_by_text: dict[str,str]) -> list[str] — returns unmatched keys, never silently drops them
_count_checklist(body: str) -> tuple[int, int] — (total_unique, done_unique), whole-body scan, fence-stripped, text-deduped with done-wins
task-document-schema.description: Typed Python representation of the open_tasks.document JSON column (epic:f42b6958, adopted per task:2f275e17). Plain dataclasses (TaskDocument/Grooming/Risk/GroomingAccuracy/Introspection/IntrospectionReport/Implementation/Related) with to_json()/from_json()/to_dict(), not pydantic — matches the repo's existing convention of plain-dict domain objects rather than adding a validation-layer dependency. schema_version=1 field allows future migration without touching every existing row. Namespaces: grooming (wholesale-replace each pass), introspection.reports[] (append-only history), implementation.progress (task:4d3a6fc5 — auto-derived checklist tally, always-overwrite, no history), related (additive/deduped reference lists). Body stays focused on Type/Task/Motivation/Resolution/Files (including the human-readable checklist itself); structured grooming/introspection/implementation-progress/decision-reference data lives in this column instead, read/written exclusively through src/tools/tasks.py's handle_update_document (grooming/introspection/related) or handle_update (implementation, recomputed automatically) — never direct SQL.
evidence: src/tools/task_document.py: TaskDocument, Grooming, Risk, GroomingAccuracy, Introspection, IntrospectionReport, Implementation, Related dataclasses
src/tools/tasks.py: _get_document(), _set_document(), handle_update_document(), _count_checklist(), handle_update() — the only read/write paths for this column
tests/test_task_document.py: TestRisk, TestGroomingGradeRisks, TestImplementation, TestTaskDocumentDefaults, TestFromJsonNullHandling, TestRoundTrip
invariants: TaskDocument.from_json(None or '') returns a fresh empty TaskDocument, never raises — every open_tasks row has no document until something writes one, so NULL must be a valid, ordinary input, not an error path (task:74dad096's backward-compatibility requirement).
Grooming.grade_risks()/handle_update_document's graded_risks param must NEVER touch last_run_at or any other Grooming field besides the matched Risk.graded values (task:3c46c40d).

handle_update_document's `grooming` param REPLACES document.grooming WHOLESALE (task:74dad096) — anything worth preserving from a prior pass must be copied into prior_art explicitly before the overwrite.
document.introspection.reports[] is APPEND-only (unlike grooming) — accumulates real history across multiple retrospectives on the same task.

Related.merge() is additive/deduped per list (commits/memories/concepts/decision_event_ids) — both /task-grooming and /task-introspection write to document.related independently without erasing what the other added.

Risk.graded is restricted to {'materialized', 'avoided', 'wrong', None} — 'missed' is deliberately not valid; it belongs in IntrospectionReport.missed_surprises. Grooming.hidden_assumptions is informational only, never graded.

document.implementation.progress (task:4d3a6fc5) is a DERIVED tally, not a copy of the body's Resolution: checklist — the checklist itself stays in the body as the single human-readable source of truth. Recomputed unconditionally inside handle_update from whatever body ends up stored (idempotent parse via _count_checklist), independent of whether the `body` param was passed that call. Does NOT go through handle_update_document — it's the one namespace written from handle_update instead, since it derives from the body handle_update already owns.

_count_checklist() dedupes checklist items by TEXT using a dict (text -> checked bool, OR-merged) — explicitly not a set of (text, checked) tuples, which would fail to dedup a line appearing both checked and unchecked. Fenced code blocks (```...```) are stripped before scanning so example checklist lines in documentation aren't counted.
task-document-schema.name: task-document-schema

contracts: handle_update(id, title='', body='', status='', issue_type='', tags='') -> {ok, id, status, issue_type, tags} — no groomed/document-adjacent flags as of task:5e2a3216 (mark_groomed moved to handle_update_document)
_task_row(row)/_task_row_full(row) include groomed_at and introspected_at (None if never run)
handle_list's TOON/json output includes groomed_at and introspected_at in the uniform row schema
_ensure_db() creates open_tasks, task_events, commit_task_map, AND task_edges by executing schema.py's DDL constants — all four tables production code depends on

handle_update_document(id, grooming=None, graded_risks=None, introspection_report=None, related=None, mark_groomed=False) -> {ok, id, document: dict, groomed: bool, unmatched_risk_grades?: list[str]} — only touches the namespaces/flags passed; sets introspected_at when introspection_report is not None, sets groomed_at when mark_groomed is True (task:5e2a3216, folded in from handle_update to remove a two-tool ambiguity during /task-grooming)
_task_row_full(row) additionally includes document: dict — handle_get is the only reader of the full document
handle_update recomputes and writes document.implementation on every call via _count_checklist(new_body) — a side effect of handle_update, not a separate MCP param
tasks-db-schema-and-migration.description: open_tasks/task_events/commit_task_map/task_edges schema and migrations for proj_tasks.db, the task management DB. Includes the groomed_at TIMESTAMP column (task:46634a19), the introspected_at TIMESTAMP column (task:e3a0233b), and the document TEXT DEFAULT NULL column (epic:f42b6958, task:544a21c0) storing a JSON-serialized TaskDocument (see task_document.py's own concept). As of task:1310d3a3, src/db/schema.py IS the single structural source of truth for these 4 tables (DDL + column-existence migration) — src/tools/tasks.py's _ensure_db() executes schema.py's DDL constants and calls schema.py's migrate_tasks_db() directly, rather than maintaining a parallel duplicate copy (the prior task:9d3acbef-era split, guarded only by a parity test, is gone).
evidence: src/tools/tasks.py: _ensure_db() — imports and executes OPEN_TASKS_DDL/TASK_EVENTS_DDL/TASK_EDGES_DDL/COMMIT_TASK_MAP_DDL from src.db.schema, calls schema.migrate_tasks_db(conn)
src/db/schema.py: OPEN_TASKS_DDL, TASK_EVENTS_DDL, TASK_EDGES_DDL, COMMIT_TASK_MAP_DDL, migrate_tasks_db() — the actual production structural path now, not test-fixture-only

tests/test_task_issue_type.py: TestSchemaParity (column-equality now true by construction, kept as cheap drift guard), TestBackfillAndNormalization (real regression coverage for what stays tasks.py-only), TestIntrospectedAt, TestGroomedAt (mark_groomed tests now call handle_update_document, task:5e2a3216)
src/tools/tasks.py: _get_document(), _set_document(), handle_update_document() — document column read/write, uses TaskDocument.from_json/to_json
src/tools/tasks.py: _count_checklist(), Implementation import — handle_update recomputes document.implementation.progress on every call (task:4d3a6fc5)
invariants: src/db/schema.py's DDL constants + migrate_tasks_db() ARE now the production structural path for proj_tasks.db (task:1310d3a3) — tasks.py's _ensure_db() executes them directly rather than duplicating. The prior invariant here (schema.py is NOT the prod path, task:9d3acbef) is SUPERSEDED; that task explicitly rejected wholesale consolidation for a broader reason (repo-wide self-healing-per-connect convention across memory.py/scratch.py/hooks.py/tasks.py) but didn't evaluate this narrower tasks.py↔schema.py-only version, which doesn't touch the other 3 modules.

What does NOT move to schema.py: BACKFILL (computing values for newly-added columns — keywords via _extract_keywords, parent_id via _extract_parent_id) and the wip/active→open status normalization. These depend on tasks.py's own helpers; moving them into schema.py would create a circular import (schema.py would need to import from tasks.py, which already imports schema.py's DDL). _ensure_db() snapshots open_tasks/task_events columns BEFORE calling migrate_tasks_db(), so it knows which columns were newly-added and only backfills those.

Any new open_tasks/task_events/task_edges/commit_task_map column or table now needs to be added to schema.py ONLY (single source) — tasks.py picks it up automatically via the DDL constants + migrate_tasks_db() it already calls. Only add tasks.py-side code if the new column also needs a VALUE backfill (like keywords/parent_id did).

task_edges was missing entirely from tasks.py's self-healing _ensure_db() until task:9d3acbef; commit_task_map had no schema.py DDL constant at all until task:1310d3a3 added COMMIT_TASK_MAP_DDL as part of this consolidation.

groomed_at is set via handle_update_document(id, mark_groomed=True) as of task:5e2a3216 (2026-07-27) — moved off handle_update, which previously carried this flag alongside unrelated title/body/status/tags edits, causing a two-tool ambiguity during /task-grooming's structured-write steps. Staleness still detected by comparing groomed_at against updated_at.
groomed_at is added inside _task_row() unconditionally, always present for TOON's uniform-header requirement. introspected_at follows the same unconditional-presence pattern.

document follows the same NULL-safe contract as every other column here: TaskDocument.from_json(None) returns a fresh empty TaskDocument, no migration/backfill needed. document is excluded from _task_row() (list/search) — only _task_row_full() (handle_get) decodes and includes it.

handle_update UNCONDITIONALLY recomputes document.implementation.progress on every call (task:4d3a6fc5). This is the ONE document-adjacent write left on handle_update rather than handle_update_document — it's a derived tally from the body handle_update already owns, not a caller-supplied flag like mark_groomed was.

introspected_at (task:e3a0233b) and groomed_at (task:5e2a3216) are both now set from inside handle_update_document — introspected_at automatically whenever introspection_report is passed (no separate flag, since passing the report already is the definitive signal), groomed_at via the explicit mark_groomed flag (no report-shaped payload exists for grooming to key off of the same way).
tasks-db-schema-and-migration.name: tasks-db-schema-and-migration

contracts: toon_cell(value) -> str: stringifies value, wraps in double quotes with internal quotes doubled if it contains a comma, newline, or quote character
rows_to_toon(rows: list[dict]) -> str: returns 'rows[0]{}:' for an empty list, otherwise 'rows[N]{field1,field2,...}:' header line followed by one two-space-indented comma-joined line per row
toon-encoding-shared-module.description: Shared TOON (Token-Oriented Object Notation) encoder for MCP tool responses that return arrays of uniform-schema dicts. Extracted from src/tools/hooks.py (task:d2165715) so src/tools/tasks.py's handle_list (task:4b5bf21f) could reuse it without duplicating the comma/quote/newline escaping logic.
invariants: Only worth using for a list of dicts sharing the same keys, returned to an LLM caller rather than a human reading raw output — nested/heterogeneous data (e.g. concept_store/concepts.json entries) loses to plain JSON under TOON, so this is not a blanket replacement for JSON responses repo-wide.

rows_to_toon() uses the FIRST row's keys as the header and does not fill in missing keys for later rows — callers MUST normalize every row to an identical, consistent key set before calling it, or the tabular header will not match later rows (handle_list in src/tools/tasks.py does this for the optional _context_only field, defaulting it to False on every row).

Any existing MCP tool being defaulted to TOON output must have its internal (non-MCP, in-process Python) callers grepped for and updated to pass format="json" explicitly — the unit test suite alone is not sufficient signal for this, since unit tests typically only exercise the tool module directly, not other in-process callers integrating with it (discovered task:4b5bf21f: hooks/ui/routes.py called tasks.py's handle_list() directly in 5 places expecting list[dict], only caught by the integration suite at deploy time, not the unit gate).
toon-encoding-shared-module.name: toon-encoding-shared-module

contracts: LoadTaskCodeNode.__call__ resolves .code_embeddings.tvim/.meta.json from Path(state['cwd']) first
LoadRelatedCommitsNode._resolve_diff_index(cwd) resolves .diff_embeddings.tvim/.meta.json from Path(cwd) first, returns (index, meta)
Both fall back to a hardcoded claude-hooks default path only when no index exists at the cwd-derived path
ups-nodes-cwd-first-repo-resolution.description: Repeated pattern across UPS task-context fan-out nodes: any node resolving a repo-scoped index/resource must try state['cwd']'s repo first, falling back to a hardcoded default repo (claude-hooks) only if nothing exists at cwd. LoadTaskCodeNode (langchain_learning/nodes/load_task_code.py) established this; LoadRelatedCommitsNode (langchain_learning/nodes/load_related_commits.py) was fixed to match it in task:4b7ccfe8 after being found to always query claude-hooks' diff index regardless of the active task's actual repo.
invariants: A task can be activated from any repo, not just claude-hooks — a node that skips the cwd check silently returns data from the wrong repo instead of failing loudly or returning empty
cwd-derived resolution is tried first and only falls back to the default repo path if the cwd-scoped resource is missing, never the other way around
New UPS nodes that read a repo-local file/index (TurboVec .tvim, git log, etc.) must follow this same resolution order
ups-nodes-cwd-first-repo-resolution.name: ups-nodes-cwd-first-repo-resolution
